entries.test: Public evaluations of the Sora version discussed, testing physical consistency across varied scenes, would establish whether it reliably models physical behavior.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give 'learned physics' a concrete reading about physical consistency.

entries.test: A representative sample of contemporaneous Sora outputs evaluated for visible anatomical, spatial, and visual errors would test its claimed limited visual reliability.
entries.note: 'At best' sets an upper bound; it does not express a probability.

entries.test: Public object-permanence evaluations, model documentation, and controlled comparisons of pixel prediction with physical-state modeling would test both the recurring failures and their proposed cause.
entries.note: The claim includes an explanation of why objects appear and disappear, making it causal.

entries.test: Public technical analyses of the contemporaneous Sora model and controlled physical-consistency tests would establish whether it models physical dynamics or constrains depicted entities to physical laws.
entries.note: The categorical wording is testable, although individual flawed videos alone cannot establish the absence of all physical modeling.

entries.test: Public anatomical-error evaluations and controlled studies of Sora's structural representations would test whether missing anatomical models cause the cited errors.
entries.note: Output errors establish the symptoms; the causal explanation requires additional technical evidence.

entries.test: Representative public evaluations of physical and biological violations, together with controlled comparisons incorporating physical simulation, would test the claimed frequency and cause.
entries.note: 'A large fraction' lacks a numerical cutoff but has a plain reading of widespread basic failures.

entries.test: Public analyses of Sora's object representations and controlled cases that pit image-sequence prediction against physical consistency would test the asserted mechanism and universal priority.
entries.note: The passage explains the asserted priority through what Sora represents; its condition describes present behavior, not a future event.

entries.test: Public technical documentation and model analyses would test whether Sora's frame prediction implements physical modeling, the distinction asserted in context.
entries.note: The source affirmatively calls prediction a fine approximation for some purposes; 'may be' weakens that commitment. Its colloquial ending still asserts a substantive technical distinction.
